description: Build the custom React Three Fiber WebGL engine that consumes the FEAT-002 state layer, and the dark-mode HUD overlay, then wire them into app/network/page.tsx and REMOVE the react-force-graph-3d NetworkGraph.tsx. The engine renders all nodes via a single THREE.InstancedMesh (one icosahedron, one draw call) with custom instanced buffer attributes (color, impact, freshness, selected) and a custom node shader (emissive glow from freshness, size from impact, selection highlight, GPU-side); edges via instanced/fat lines (Line2/LineSegments2 from three-stdlib) with a flow shader (causal edges animate cause->effect, semantic dimmer/static); SDF labels via troika-three-text with frustum+distance+importance LOD capped at ~50 visible; time-axis Z depth projection with distance fog; eased camera transitions (camera-controls) on zoom-into-cluster; semantic LOD collapsing low-impact nodes into cluster impostors when zoomed out. React MUST NOT reconcile 3D nodes: the <Canvas> subtree uses useFrame to consume the store's dirty ranges and push them to GPU buffers, with frameloop='demand' + invalidate() so the GPU idles when static. Explicit dispose() of geometries/materials/textures on teardown. React only renders the HUD DOM overlay.
steps: Create components/graph3d/GraphScene.tsx: the <Canvas> subtree (client component, dynamic import with ssr:false to match the current NetworkGraph pattern). Set frameloop='demand'. Inside, an InstancedNodes component builds ONE THREE.InstancedMesh from an IcosahedronGeometry sized to the store CAPACITY, with instanced buffer attributes for color/impact/freshness/selected, and a custom ShaderMaterial (or onBeforeCompile-patched MeshStandardMaterial) implementing emissive glow from freshness, scale from impact, and selection highlight fully GPU-side. A useFrame callback consumes store.consumeDirtyRange(), copies the touched slice into instanceMatrix/instanceColor/custom attributes, sets needsUpdate only on the touched attributes, and calls invalidate() when work was done. Hoist ALL Vector3/Matrix4/Color/Quaternion scratch objects to module or ref scope - ZERO per-frame allocation in the hot path.

Create components/graph3d/InstancedEdges.tsx: render edges as fat lines using LineSegments2/LineSegmentsGeometry + LineMaterial (three-stdlib) OR a single BufferGeometry of line segments, with a custom flow shader. Causal-relationship edges animate directionally (cause->effect flow); semantic edges are static and dimmer. Positions update from the store's edge/position arrays via useFrame on dirty ranges. Highlight edges connected to the selected node (reuse the connected-edge concept from the old NetworkGraph).

Create components/graph3d/GraphLabels.tsx: SDF text via troika-three-text. Compute visible labels each frame with LOD = frustum cull + camera distance + node importance (impact/freshness); cap the visible set to ~50 regardless of graph size (pool/reuse Text instances, do not allocate per frame). Labels show the node title (truncated).

Create components/graph3d/CameraRig.tsx: integrate camera-controls (or drei's CameraControls) for eased dolly transitions to a cluster centroid or selected node on zoom-into-cluster / node click. Apply distance fog and the time-axis Z depth projection (older articles recede on Z) at the scene level.

Implement semantic LOD: when zoomed out beyond a threshold, collapse low-impact nodes into per-cluster hull/impostor representations (e.g. a larger instanced sphere per category cluster) and expand back to individual nodes on zoom-in. Keep this GPU/attribute-driven where possible; document any CPU work and ensure it stays off the per-frame allocation path.

Create the HUD overlay as plain React DOM (NOT inside <Canvas>) in components/graph3d/GraphHUD.tsx and sub-panels, subscribing to store slices via selectors: (a) InspectorDrawer - reuse the existing node-detail panel content from the old NetworkGraph.tsx (headline, image with category-gradient fallback, source, summary, tags, freshness bar/badge, Visit Article link, related-nodes chips); (b) EntityFilters - filter by sector/category/entity/sentiment/time, wired to store.setFilters which drives BOTH the worker-sim visibility AND (in FEAT-004) the WS subscription predicate; (c) SentimentHeatmap overlay - a legend/overlay coloring by the sentiment derivation; (d) EventSequenceTimeline - a scrub/time-window control feeding the time filter. Use the existing design system (glass-premium, lime/emerald, charcoal, Inter) so it matches the current look.

Rewrite app/network/page.tsx to render the new GraphScene + GraphHUD instead of <NetworkGraph>. On mount, do the existing initial REST load via useGraphData() (GET /api/graph) and call store.initFromGraph(graphData); start the FEAT-002 force-sim worker. Keep the existing header, DataSourceBadge, freshness legend, node/connection counts, and TopicCorrelationsPanel. The page must render correctly with the current data sources (live/cached/sample) and with no backend/WS configured.

DELETE components/NetworkGraph.tsx and remove the react-force-graph-3d dependency from package.json (and its usage). Confirm nothing else imports NetworkGraph or react-force-graph-3d (grep). Removing this file should also remove the two pre-existing lint warnings.

Ensure explicit teardown: GraphScene and its children dispose() all geometries, materials, shaders, textures, and troika Text instances on unmount and when the graph is re-initialized, so filter toggles and navigation do not leak (the class of bug the prototype had).

Add a headless canvas-mount smoke test: using Playwright (available as a Kiro power) against a bounded `next start` (build first; do NOT background `next dev`), navigate to /network and assert the <canvas> element mounts and no uncaught console errors / thrown exceptions occur during scene init. If a real WebGL context is unavailable in the headless sandbox, fall back to a jsdom render test that mounts GraphScene with a stubbed/mock WebGL context and asserts it initializes without throwing. Document which path was used and what still requires a real GPU (frame rate, visual correctness).
acceptance_criteria: All graph nodes render through a SINGLE THREE.InstancedMesh (one icosahedron geometry, one draw call) with custom instanced attributes and a custom shader driving glow/size/selection GPU-side.
Edges render as fat/instanced lines with a flow shader; causal edges animate directionally and semantic edges are static/dimmer.
Labels use troika-three-text SDF with LOD (frustum + distance + importance) capped at ~50 visible regardless of graph size.

The <Canvas> uses frameloop='demand' + invalidate(); React does not reconcile individual 3D nodes - node/edge/position updates flow via useFrame consuming the store's dirty ranges; no per-frame heap allocation in the hot path (scratch objects hoisted).
Camera transitions are eased (camera-controls); time-axis Z depth projection + distance fog present; semantic LOD collapses/expands clusters on zoom.

The HUD (inspector drawer, entity filters, sentiment heatmap, event-sequence timeline) renders as DOM outside the Canvas, subscribes via store selectors, matches the existing dark design system, and filters drive the worker-sim visibility.
components/NetworkGraph.tsx and the react-force-graph-3d dependency are removed; nothing imports them; app/network/page.tsx uses the new engine.
Geometries/materials/textures/Text are explicitly disposed on teardown/re-init.
`bun run build` succeeds; `bun run lint` is clean (the two old NetworkGraph warnings are gone with the file); `bun test` still passes.

A headless canvas-mount smoke test asserts the scene initializes without errors (via Playwright on `next start`, or a stubbed-WebGL jsdom render), with GPU-dependent aspects explicitly documented as needing a real browser.
verification: Run `bun run build` and confirm exit 0.
Run `bun run lint` and confirm it is clean with no NetworkGraph warnings remaining.
Run `bun test` and confirm all unit tests + the canvas-mount smoke test pass.
Run `grep -rn "react-force-graph-3d\|components/NetworkGraph" app components lib` and confirm no matches remain.
